question: The ward records are kept mainly to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. provide a complete account of the care given and the course of each patient

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The records give a full account of the patient's condition, the care given and the response, and they serve for the next shift, for the doctor and for any later enquiry

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — fill the cupboards of the office: Records are not kept to fill cupboards

B — satisfy the visiting relatives: Relatives' satisfaction is not the purpose

D — increase the work of the nurse: Records add work but their value is clinical and legal

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse writes the record so that a colleague who has never seen the patient can continue the care from it alone, because that is the test of a good record
option_3: provide a complete account of the care given and the course of each patient

question: In a ward, inventory means:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. the detailed list of the articles held in stock with their quantities

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An inventory is the item by item list of what the ward holds and how much of each is present

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the list of the nurses on duty: The duty list is a roster

B — the list of the drugs given: The drugs given are recorded on the drug chart

C — the list of the patients admitted: The list of patients is the admission register

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse in charge checks one section of the inventory each week rather than the whole at the month end, because a shortage found in the first week can still be traced and a shortage found at the end of the month cannot
option_1: the list of the nurses on duty
option_4: the detailed list of the articles held in stock with their quantities

question: A nursing officer finds that a few costly items of the ward store are used up far faster than the rest. The sound step is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. keep a closer watch on the costly fast moving items, since they make up most of the value of the store

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A small number of items usually accounts for most of the value in a store, so these are watched and controlled most closely

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — buy the cheapest substitutes: Substituting cheap articles can lower the standard of care

B — stop buying all the items: Stopping the purchase of all the items stops the work

C — ignore them as they are small in number: Ignoring them because they are few in number is exactly the mistake, since their value is high

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse keeps a separate record for these items with the date and the quantity issued, because the cost of the whole store is decided by a handful of costly articles
option_3: ignore them as they are small in number
option_4: keep a closer watch on the costly fast moving items, since they make up most of the value of the store

question: The reorder level of an item in the ward store is the quantity at which:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a fresh order must be placed so that the stock does not run out before it arrives

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The reorder level allows for the time taken to obtain the item, so that it does not run out while the order is coming

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the item is thrown away: Discarding has nothing to do with the reorder level

C — the item is counted: Counting is done at the stock taking

D — the price of the item is revised: The price is not the concern of the level

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse fixes the reorder level a little above the average use during the delivery time, because a level set exactly at the average is certain to run out in a busy week
option_1: a fresh order must be placed so that the stock does not run out before it arrives
option_4: the price of the item is revised

question: A 60-bed ward must issue linen from the store. The nurse in charge should follow the rule of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. first in first out, so that the older stock is used before the newer

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The older stock is issued first so that nothing becomes stale or expires while newer stock is being used

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — last in first out: Last in first out leaves the older stock to spoil

B — keeping the oldest stock aside for an emergency: Stock kept aside for an emergency is the stock that expires

C — issuing the newest stock first: Issuing the newest first is the same fault in another form

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse writes the date of receipt on each pack as it is stacked behind the older ones, because a store arranged by date is safe without any memory work at all
option_2: keeping the oldest stock aside for an emergency
option_4: first in first out, so that the older stock is used before the newer

question: NABH, in the context of a hospital, stands for the body that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. accredits hospitals against set standards of quality and patient safety

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers assesses a hospital against published standards and grants accreditation when they are met

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — conducts the nursing examinations: Examinations are the work of the nursing councils and the universities

C — fixes the pay of the nurses: Pay is fixed by the employer or the government and not by this body

D — supplies the drugs to the hospital: Supply of drugs is not its work

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse keeps the records complete and the equipment in working order long before the assessment, because accreditation is granted on the day to day practice of the ward and not on the files prepared in the last week
option_1: accredits hospitals against set standards of quality and patient safety

question: A quality indicator in a hospital ward is best described as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. a number that measures how far the care meets a set standard

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An indicator is a measurable signal, such as the rate of falls or of infection, that shows whether the care is reaching the standard set for it

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the age of the building: The age of the building says nothing about the care given in it

C — the number of doctors in the ward: The number of doctors is a resource and not an outcome

D — the cost of the ward per day: Cost is a matter of budget and not of quality

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records falls, pressure sores and drug errors in a simple monthly chart, because an indicator that is never counted is only an opinion
option_2: a number that measures how far the care meets a set standard
option_3: the number of doctors in the ward
option_4: the cost of the ward per day

question: A near miss in a hospital ward is best described as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. an event that could have harmed a patient but did not reach the patient

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A near miss is an error that was caught in time, so no harm reached the patient, and it is studied because it shows where the system is weak

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a delay in the discharge of a patient: A delay in discharge is a process matter and not a near miss

B — an error that has harmed the patient: An event that has actually harmed the patient is an adverse event

D — a complaint received from a relative: A complaint is a report of dissatisfaction and not a near miss

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reports near misses as readily as actual harms, because a near miss is the free warning that tells the ward where the next real error will occur
option_1: a delay in the discharge of a patient
option_2: an error that has harmed the patient
option_3: an event that could have harmed a patient but did not reach the patient

question: The chief purpose of supervision of the nursing staff is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. guide, support and improve the work of the staff so that the care is safe

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Supervision guides the staff, helps them do the work correctly and supports them where they are weak

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — write the confidential reports: Confidential reports are a separate duty

B — reduce the work of the senior nurse: Supervision adds work rather than reducing it

D — find out the faults of the staff: Finding faults is not its purpose, though shortcomings are corrected

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The senior nurse supervises at the bedside and not from the office, because a difficulty is understood only when the work is seen as it is actually done
option_2: reduce the work of the senior nurse
option_3: guide, support and improve the work of the staff so that the care is safe
option_4: find out the faults of the staff

question: A nurse in charge delegates a dressing to a junior nurse. The rule of delegation requires that the junior nurse:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. has the skill to do the task and the authority to do it

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A task may be delegated only to a person trained for it and given the authority to do it, and the senior remains answerable for the result

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — may further delegate it to the ward boy: A task given to a nurse cannot be passed on to an untrained person

C — works under the direct eyes of the senior: Direct watching is required only while the person is still learning

D — is the same grade as the senior: The grade need not be the same, for a junior may be fully able to do the task

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The senior states what is to be done and the limits within which it is to be done, because a task given without limits leaves the junior unsure when to call for help
option_1: may further delegate it to the ward boy
option_2: has the skill to do the task and the authority to do it
option_3: works under the direct eyes of the senior
option_4: is the same grade as the senior

question: While issuing vaccines from the ward refrigerator the nurse finds one vial past its expiry date. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. remove it from the stock at once, record it and send it for disposal as per the rules

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An expired vial is removed from the stock at once, entered in the record and destroyed by the proper method, since a vaccine past its date has lost its power

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — keep it back for use in an emergency: Keeping it for an emergency is the same fault with a reason attached

C — return it to the store without informing anyone: A quiet return leaves the wrong record and may bring the vial back into circulation

D — issue it since a little delay does no harm: Using it gives false protection and wastes the session

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse checks the dates of the whole stock on the first day of every month, because a vial found past its date during a session is one that has to be discarded in front of a waiting family
option_1: remove it from the stock at once, record it and send it for disposal as per the rules
option_2: keep it back for use in an emergency
option_3: return it to the store without informing anyone
option_4: issue it since a little delay does no harm

question: A 70-year-old patient is given a unit of blood of the wrong group and dies. For the hospital this occurrence is a:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. sentinel event that must be reported at once and studied in detail

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An unexpected occurrence that causes death or serious harm is a sentinel event, and it is reported at once and studied so that the cause is removed

🔍 Key Clues: 70-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — matter for the patient's family alone: The hospital is answerable as well as the family concerned

C — matter that need not be recorded: An unrecorded event cannot be studied and repeats itself

D — minor incident to be entered in the ward register only: An event of this gravity cannot be closed with a ward note

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse takes part in the study of the event as a member of the team and not as an accused person, because in a review that looks for a person to blame the next error is simply never reported
option_1: sentinel event that must be reported at once and studied in detail
option_4: minor incident to be entered in the ward register only

question: The nursing hours per patient per day is worked out by the nursing officer mainly to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. fix the salary of the nurses

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The total nursing hours needed by all the patients, divided by the hours one nurse works, gives the number of nurses required for the ward

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — decide the visiting hours: Visiting hours are a separate matter

B — decide the number of nurses the ward needs: Salaries are fixed by the employer and not by this figure

D — count the beds in the ward: Counting beds does not measure the care needed

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse revises the calculation whenever the patient mix changes, because a ward that has become heavier in its work needs more nurses even though the number of beds is exactly the same
option_2: decide the number of nurses the ward needs

question: At the month end the nurse in charge finds that the register shows 40 packets of gauze but the shelf holds only 32. The correct step is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. count again with a second nurse, look into the issue slips and report the difference instead of changing the record

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A second count by two nurses, a search of the issue slips and an honest report is the correct way to settle a difference

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — borrow eight packets from another ward and say nothing: Borrowing quietly shifts the shortage to another ward

B — leave the matter to the next month: Leaving it to the next month allows the gap to widen

C — alter the register to show 32: Altering the register hides the loss and destroys the record

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse writes the reason for the difference and the action taken on the same sheet, because a balance that has been made to agree artificially leaves no trace for the next nurse in charge to follow
option_1: borrow eight packets from another ward and say nothing
option_2: leave the matter to the next month
option_4: count again with a second nurse, look into the issue slips and report the difference instead of changing the record

question: Before asking for a costly piece of equipment for the ward the nursing officer should first:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. work out the need for it, the number of patients who will benefit and the cost against the benefit

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A proposal is supported by the need, the expected use and the cost compared with the benefit, and this is what makes it worth funding

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — wait for the equipment to be donated: Waiting for a donation leaves the need unmet

B — ask the staff what they would like: A wish list is not a case for the equipment

D — place the order to save time: An order placed before the case is made is the one that is struck out

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse mentions the number of patients and the hours of nursing time the equipment will save, because a figure in patients and hours is what moves a budget committee
option_1: wait for the equipment to be donated
option_2: ask the staff what they would like
option_3: work out the need for it, the number of patients who will benefit and the cost against the benefit

question: In research the whole group about which the researcher wishes to draw a conclusion is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. population

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The population is the entire group of interest, such as all the nurses of a state, from which the sample is drawn

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — variable: A variable is a characteristic that is measured

B — sample: The sample is the smaller part of it that is actually studied

D — control group: The control group is one arm of an experiment

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse states the population in clear words before choosing the sample, because a study of one ward cannot be used to speak about the nurses of the whole country

question: Data such as the sex of the patient and the blood group are called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. categorical data

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Categorical, or qualitative, data fall into named groups, and they are counted rather than measured

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — continuous data: Continuous data can take any value within a range, such as weight

B — interval data: Interval data are ordered numbers with equal gaps, such as temperature in degrees

C — ratio data: Ratio data have a true zero, such as height

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse counts the patients in each group for such data and does not average them, because a mean of two blood groups has no meaning at all

question: To study the hand washing practice of nurses of four different grades, the researcher picks a fixed number from each grade. This is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. stratified sampling

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The population is first divided into strata, here the grades, and a fixed number is drawn from each, which is stratified sampling

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — convenience sampling: Convenience sampling takes whoever is easiest to reach

B — snowball sampling: Snowball sampling grows through the contacts of those already chosen

D — simple random sampling: Simple random sampling draws from the whole list without dividing it

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse writes down the strata before drawing the sample, because a sample that draws everyone from one shift gives a picture of that shift and not of the ward

question: From a list of 100 patients the researcher picks number 5, then 15, then 25 and so on. This method is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. systematic sampling

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Choosing every tenth name from a list is systematic sampling, which is simple to carry out and spreads evenly over the list

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — cluster sampling: Cluster sampling selects whole groups, such as entire wards

B — quota sampling: Quota sampling fills set numbers in each group

D — purposive sampling: Purposive sampling picks members the researcher judges suitable

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse starts the list at a number chosen at random, because a list that is already arranged in some order can make a fixed starting point give a one sided sample

question: A 30-year-old researcher studies hand hygiene by standing only at the main door of a ward, and reports that all the nurses of the hospital wash their hands well. The main weakness of this study is that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the sample was drawn from one place only and does not represent the whole hospital

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A sample taken from one ward cannot be used to speak about every nurse of the hospital, however well the observation itself was done

🔍 Key Clues: 30-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the study took too little time: The time taken is not the weakness of the design here

C — the researcher was too young: The age of the researcher has no bearing on the method

D — hand washing cannot be studied at all: Hand washing can be studied well by direct observation

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reports the sample and the setting along with the result, because a conclusion that is drawn wider than the sample allows is the commonest fault in a small study
option_2: the sample was drawn from one place only and does not represent the whole hospital
option_4: hand washing cannot be studied at all

question: A weighing scale that gives the same weight every time it is used, but is set wrongly by two kilograms, is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. reliable but not valid

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A reliable tool gives the same reading each time, but if it is wrongly set it does not measure the true value and so is not valid

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — both reliable and valid: It is not valid, so it cannot be both

B — valid but not reliable: A valid tool measures the truth, and this one does not

D — neither reliable nor valid: It is reliable, so this option is wrong

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse checks the scale against a known weight at the start of every clinic, because a tool that is consistent but wrong gives a whole day's figures that are all wrong together

question: Before the main study a nurse tries the questionnaire on ten colleagues to see whether the questions are understood. This step is a:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. pilot study

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A pilot study is a small trial run on a few people to test the tool and to find the difficulties before the main study begins

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — literature review: A literature review is the reading of earlier work

B — final report: A final report comes at the end

C — hypothesis: A hypothesis is the statement to be tested

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse notes the time each person takes and the questions they ask back, because a question that needed explaining in the pilot will need explaining fifty times in the main study

question: Compared with a written questionnaire, an interview is better when:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the questions are deep and the answers need to be probed

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In an interview the researcher can explain a question, ask again and follow up an answer, which is what a deep subject needs

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the time available is very short: An interview takes more time and not less

C — the sample is very large and far away: A large far away sample is better reached by post

D — the researcher cannot meet the people: An interview needs the people to be met

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse keeps the interview to a set time and writes the answers at once, because a long interview tires the patient and answers written from memory later lose the words the patient actually used
option_2: the questions are deep and the answers need to be probed
option_3: the sample is very large and far away

question: A researcher uses the mean and the standard deviation to summarise the data. These belong to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. descriptive statistics

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The mean and the standard deviation describe the collected data themselves and are called descriptive statistics

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — coding of the data: Coding is the way the data are entered for analysis

C — inferential statistics: Inferential statistics use the sample to draw a conclusion about the population, as in a test of significance

D — the sampling method: The sampling method is a part of the design

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reports the standard deviation along with the mean, because two wards may have the same average stay while one of them has a few very long stays that change the whole picture

question: The ages of five patients are 22, 26, 30, 34 and 38 years. The mean age is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 30 years

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The total is one hundred and fifty years, and divided by five this gives thirty years

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 34 years: 34 years is the fourth age in the list

C — 28 years: 28 years is below the true mean

D — 32 years: 32 years is above the true mean

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: Add the values and count them before dividing, because dividing before the total is complete is the commonest slip in a mean

question: In a study of 100 patients the mean length of stay is 8 days with a standard deviation of 1 day. The nurse understands that most of the patients stayed:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. close to 8 days, most of them between 7 and 9 days

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A small standard deviation means the values cluster closely about the mean, so most patients stayed within one day on either side of eight days

🔍 Key Clues: 8 days | 1 day

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — between 1 and 8 days: The standard deviation is one day and not eight

B — for more than 15 days: A stay of more than fifteen days would be far outside this spread

C — exactly 8 days each: A mean of 8 does not mean that every patient stayed exactly eight days

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reads the standard deviation before quoting the mean to the office, because an average with a wide spread describes a ward that is very different from one with the same average and a narrow spread
option_4: close to 8 days, most of them between 7 and 9 days

question: In a study the result shows a p value of 0.30. The nurse understands that this means:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the difference found could easily have arisen by chance, so it is not significant

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A p value above the accepted level of 0.05 means the difference observed could well have come about by chance and is not taken as significant

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the sample was wrongly chosen: The p value says nothing about the choice of the sample

C — the study has proved nothing at all about anything: The study may still describe the data usefully even when the difference is not significant

D — the result is highly significant: A small p value, not a large one, shows significance

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reports the p value and not only the word significant, because a claim of significance without the figure behind it cannot be checked by anyone else
option_2: the difference found could easily have arisen by chance, so it is not significant
option_3: the study has proved nothing at all about anything

question: A type one error in research is the error of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. rejecting a true null hypothesis, that is finding a difference where none exists

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A type one error is the rejection of a null hypothesis that is in fact true, so a difference is reported where there is none

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — failing to find a real difference: Failing to find a real difference is a type two error

C — making a mistake in the arithmetic: An arithmetic mistake is not a type one error

D — accepting a true hypothesis: Accepting a true hypothesis is the correct decision and not an error

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reads the level of significance as the risk the researcher has accepted of making this error, because a study that allows a large risk makes a claim that a ward should not yet act upon
option_1: rejecting a true null hypothesis, that is finding a difference where none exists

question: A nurse wishes to show the number of patients admitted with dengue in each month of a year. The best way to present this is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. a bar chart of the months against the number of patients

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A bar chart with the months along one axis and the number of patients along the other shows the rise and the fall across the year at a glance

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a list of the patients' names: A list of names is a record and not a presentation

C — a single line of text in the report: A line of text hides the trend

D — a pie chart of the drug costs: A pie chart shows the parts of a whole at one time and not a change month by month

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse labels both axes and writes the units, because a chart without its units is read differently by every person who sees it
option_2: a bar chart of the months against the number of patients
option_3: a single line of text in the report
option_4: a pie chart of the drug costs

question: A frequency distribution table in a report shows:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. how many persons fall into each class or category of the data

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The table arranges the values into classes and shows the number of persons in each, which is the first step in seeing the shape of the data

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the names of the researchers: The names of the researchers belong to the title page

C — the cost of the study: Cost is not a part of the data table

D — the list of references: References belong to the end of the report

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse uses classes of equal width and writes the total at the bottom, because a table whose classes differ in width makes small groups look as large as big ones
option_2: how many persons fall into each class or category of the data

question: Consent for a procedure may be taken from a parent or a guardian when the patient is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a minor or a person unable to give valid consent

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A person who cannot give valid consent, such as a minor or a patient who is unconscious, needs the consent of the parent or the guardian

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — an adult of sound mind: An adult of sound mind gives consent for himself

C — a person who has already signed a similar form: A form signed for another procedure does not cover a fresh one

D — a nurse of the same hospital: The fact of being a nurse makes no difference

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse takes consent from the person named as the guardian on the admission record, because a signature from whoever happens to be present is the one that is challenged later
option_1: a minor or a person unable to give valid consent
option_3: a person who has already signed a similar form

question: A 28-year-old man is found positive for HIV and asks the nurse not to tell his family. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. keep the information confidential, share it only with the treating team and counsel the patient about informing his partner himself

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The result is confidential, is shared only with those who need it for care, and the patient is helped and encouraged to tell his partner himself

🔍 Key Clues: 28-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — announce it at the ward meeting: A ward meeting is not a place for such a matter

C — record it on the front of the case sheet in large letters: A note in large letters on the cover exposes the patient to everyone who handles the file

D — inform the family as they have a right to know: The family has no automatic right to be told against the patient's wish

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

option_3: record it on the front of the case sheet in large letters
option_4: inform the family as they have a right to know

question: When a patient is found to have a notifiable disease, the nurse must:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. report it to the local health authority at once in the prescribed form

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A notifiable disease is reported at once to the health authority in the prescribed form, so that the source is traced and the spread is stopped

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — keep it to the ward register only: A ward register does not inform the authority

B — wait till the patient is discharged: Waiting loses the chance to control the outbreak

C — inform the neighbours: Informing the neighbours breaches confidentiality

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse sends the report the same day and keeps a copy, because the health authority counts the cases by the date of reporting and a case reported late is counted in the wrong week
option_1: keep it to the ward register only
option_4: report it to the local health authority at once in the prescribed form

question: In a claim of negligence the nurse's conduct is judged by comparing it with:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the care that a reasonably competent nurse of the same level would have given in the same situation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The standard is the conduct of a reasonably competent nurse of the same level working in the same circumstances, and not perfection

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the care given by a doctor: A nurse is compared with a nurse and not with a doctor

C — the care described in a textbook: A textbook may guide practice but does not by itself set the legal standard

D — the best possible care in the country: The law does not demand the best care in the country

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records what was actually done and why, because the record is how the nurse shows that the care given was reasonable in the circumstances that existed at the time
option_1: the care that a reasonably competent nurse of the same level would have given in the same situation
option_4: the best possible care in the country

question: The principle of res ipsa loquitur applies when:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the injury is of a kind that does not happen unless someone has been negligent

🧠 Clinical Rationale: When the thing speaks for itself, as when a patient is burnt by a hot water bottle left in the bed, negligence is presumed and the burden of explanation shifts

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the hospital has denied the incident: A denial does not remove the presumption

C — the nurse was not on duty: Being off duty does not settle the matter

D — the patient has signed a consent form: A consent form covers the procedure and not the negligence

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records the equipment used and the checks made, because in such a case a record that shows the correct care is what answers a presumption of fault
option_1: the injury is of a kind that does not happen unless someone has been negligent
option_4: the patient has signed a consent form

question: A 42-year-old man with chest pain is left alone in the ward when the nurse goes to the canteen without handing over. In law this is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. abandonment of the patient, for which the nurse is answerable

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A nurse may not leave a patient without handing the care to another competent person, and leaving one alone is abandonment

🔍 Key Clues: 42-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a matter for the ward boy: The ward boy has no responsibility for the care of the patient

C — a fault of the patient: The fault is the nurse's and not the patient's

D — an accepted break: A break is taken only after a proper handover

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse informs the person in charge before leaving the ward even for a short while, because a patient who needs help in those few minutes has no one to call
option_2: abandonment of the patient, for which the nurse is answerable

question: A nurse gives first aid at the roadside to an unconscious accident victim. In law the nurse is protected because:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. consent is implied in an emergency where life is in danger and the patient cannot consent

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In a real emergency the law takes it that a person would consent to the steps needed to save life, so the nurse may act at once

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the police are present: The presence of the police has no bearing on the consent

B — first aid is not a professional act: First aid given by a professional is judged as the act of a professional

D — the nurse is not answerable for anything done outside the hospital: A nurse remains answerable for negligent acts wherever they are done

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse gives the help that is needed and stays till the ambulance comes, because the legal protection covers the help given in a true emergency and not the act of a person who walks away
option_2: first aid is not a professional act
option_3: consent is implied in an emergency where life is in danger and the patient cannot consent
option_4: the nurse is not answerable for anything done outside the hospital

question: A gene is best described as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. a unit of heredity that carries the information for a trait

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A gene is a length of the genetic material that carries the instructions for one or more characters passed from parent to child

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a hormone of the body: A hormone is a chemical messenger and not a unit of heredity

C — a type of white blood cell: A white cell is a blood cell

D — a small organ in the cell: A gene is not an organ but a part of the genetic material

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse explains that a gene is like one line of instruction in a long book, because an image such as this is remembered by a family long after the technical words are forgotten
option_2: a unit of heredity that carries the information for a trait

question: Twins who develop from a single fertilised ovum are:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. identical twins

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Twins from one fertilised ovum have the same genes and are identical, and they are always of the same sex

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — fraternal twins: Fraternal twins come from two separate ova

B — of different sexes always: Identical twins are of the same sex and not of different sexes

D — unlike in their blood groups: Their blood groups are the same and not unlike

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse knows that the parents of identical twins often cannot tell them apart in the first weeks, so the babies are banded at birth and the bands are checked before every feed and every drug

question: A carrier of a recessive genetic disease is a person who:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. has one faulty gene but does not show the disease

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A carrier has one faulty and one normal gene, remains healthy and can pass the faulty gene to the children

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — cannot pass the gene to the children: A carrier can and does pass the gene on

B — has two faulty genes: Two faulty genes give the disease and not the carrier state

D — has the disease: A person who has both faulty genes shows the disease

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse explains the carrier state in simple words to a young couple before marriage, because the risk to the children begins with the two carriers and not with any child
option_1: cannot pass the gene to the children
option_3: has one faulty gene but does not show the disease

question: Sickle cell anaemia is caused by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. a change in the gene that makes haemoglobin

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A change in the gene for haemoglobin makes the red cells take a sickle shape, and these cells are destroyed early and block small vessels

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — an infection caught in childhood: An infection does not change the gene

B — a diet that is poor in iron: A poor diet gives iron deficiency anaemia and not this condition

C — an injury to the bone marrow: An injury to the marrow reduces the cells but does not change the shape of them

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse tells a carrier couple the risk before they plan children, and teaches a child with the disease to drink plenty of water, because dehydration makes the cells sickle and brings on a painful crisis
option_2: a diet that is poor in iron
option_4: a change in the gene that makes haemoglobin

question: The sex of a child is determined by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. the chromosome received from the father

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The mother contributes an X chromosome and the father an X or a Y, so it is the father's chromosome that decides the sex of the child

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the age of the mother: The age of the mother does not decide it

B — the chromosome received from the mother: The mother can contribute only an X chromosome

D — the diet of the mother: The diet of the mother does not decide the sex

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse knows this well enough to answer plainly when a mother is taunted by the family for bearing daughters, because a wrong belief that harms a woman and a child is not a small matter

question: A pedigree chart in genetics is used to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. trace the pattern of a trait through a family over several generations

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A pedigree, drawn with squares for males and circles for females, shows who in the family over the generations was affected, and from it the pattern of inheritance is judged

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — measure the intelligence of a family: Intelligence is not measured by a pedigree

C — count the members of a household: Counting the members is a census and not a pedigree

D — record the blood pressure of the family: Blood pressures are recorded on a clinical chart

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse draws the pedigree with the family sitting together and asks about each relative by name, because a family member remembers an aunt's illness only when she is asked about that aunt
option_2: trace the pattern of a trait through a family over several generations
option_4: record the blood pressure of the family

question: A 26-year-old woman at 8 weeks of pregnancy is prescribed a drug that is known to harm the fetus. The nurse's most important action is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. check the prescription with the doctor at once, explain the risk and ask for a safer drug

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The first eight weeks are the period of organ formation, and a known harmful drug is queried with the doctor at once so that a safer one is chosen

🔍 Key Clues: 26-year-old | 8 weeks

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — reduce the dose by half and give it: The nurse does not alter a dose on her own

C — give the drug as ordered without question: A nurse must not give a drug whose risk she has identified without checking

D — wait for the next antenatal visit: Waiting till the next visit lets the harm be done

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse also checks for a history of drugs taken before the pregnancy was known, because the harm is greatest in the very weeks in which the woman does not yet know that she is pregnant
option_1: check the prescription with the doctor at once, explain the risk and ask for a safer drug
option_2: reduce the dose by half and give it
option_3: give the drug as ordered without question

question: A 30-year-old woman is to have her abdominal wound dressed. The nurse explains the procedure first mainly to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. gain her co-operation and reduce her anxiety

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An explanation before a procedure prepares the patient, reduces fear and wins her co-operation

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — make the wound heal faster: Healing is not hastened by an explanation

B — save time during the dressing: The explanation does not shorten the task

C — avoid using gloves: Gloves are worn whatever is explained

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse explains what the patient will feel rather than only what will be done, because a patient who has been told to expect a pulling sensation is far less frightened when it comes
option_4: gain her co-operation and reduce her anxiety

question: A 65-year-old man's urine is to be sent for culture. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. collect it in a sterile container and fill the label at the bedside before sending it without delay

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A sterile container with the label filled at the bedside and prompt sending gives a report that can be trusted

🔍 Key Clues: 65-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — send it in the container used for the previous sample: A used container is contaminated

B — keep it in the refrigerator overnight: A sample kept overnight grows other organisms and is misleading

C — collect it in any clean bottle and label it later in the laboratory: A sample labelled away from the patient is a classic cause of a wrong result

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

option_1: send it in the container used for the previous sample
option_3: collect it in any clean bottle and label it later in the laboratory
option_4: collect it in a sterile container and fill the label at the bedside before sending it without delay

question: A 50-year-old man with an indwelling urinary catheter develops cloudy urine with a strong smell. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. increase his fluid intake, keep the drainage bag below the bladder and inform the doctor

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Cloudy smelly urine suggests infection, so fluids are increased, the bag is kept low to prevent backflow and the doctor is told

🔍 Key Clues: 50-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — remove the catheter without an order: Removing the catheter without an order is not the nurse's decision

B — change the bag every hour: Changing the bag every hour invites contamination

D — clamp the catheter and leave it: Clamping stops the drainage and encourages infection

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse also does the perineal care and keeps the tubing free of loops, because urine that lies about the meatus is the source from which the infection climbs
option_3: increase his fluid intake, keep the drainage bag below the bladder and inform the doctor

question: A 55-year-old man is admitted with severe central chest pain. The nurse should first:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. put him at complete rest, keep him propped up and inform the doctor at once

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Rest reduces the work of the heart, and the doctor is called at once because the pain may be a heart attack

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — ask him to take deep breaths: Deep breathing does not relieve a cardiac pain

B — give him a hot drink: A hot drink is not the treatment of such pain

D — make him walk to the X-ray room: Walking increases the load on the heart

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records the time the pain began and gives the ordered drug under the tongue, because the minutes from the onset of the pain decide the benefit of the treatment
option_3: put him at complete rest, keep him propped up and inform the doctor at once
option_4: make him walk to the X-ray room

question: A 60-year-old woman with heart failure has gained two kilograms in three days. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. check for swelling of the legs, breathlessness and a raised jugular pulse, and inform the doctor

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A sudden gain in weight in heart failure usually means fluid is collecting, so the signs of overload are looked for and the doctor is told

🔍 Key Clues: 60-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — reduce her food: Reducing food does not correct the fluid

C — increase her fluids: More fluid adds to the overload

D — record it as a normal gain: A rapid gain is not normal

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse weighs the patient at the same time each morning on the same scale, because a change of a kilogram that is really a change of scale or of clothing is worse than no measurement at all
option_2: check for swelling of the legs, breathlessness and a raised jugular pulse, and inform the doctor

question: A 45-year-old man after abdominal surgery has not passed flatus for two days and his abdomen is distended. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. listen for bowel sounds, encourage early movement, keep him nil by mouth if ordered and inform the doctor

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A distended abdomen with no flatus after abdominal surgery may mean the bowel has not yet recovered, so the bowel sounds are checked, early movement is encouraged and the doctor is informed

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — apply a tight binder: A tight binder increases the discomfort and hides the abdomen

B — give a solid meal: Solids given before the bowel works cause vomiting

C — give a large drink of cold water: A large cold drink adds to the distension

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records the passing of flatus as a landmark, because it is the sign the doctor waits for before allowing food by mouth
option_3: give a large drink of cold water
option_4: listen for bowel sounds, encourage early movement, keep him nil by mouth if ordered and inform the doctor

question: A 70-year-old man on bed rest develops a red area over the sacrum that does not turn white when pressed. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. keep the area off pressure, turn him regularly, keep the skin clean and dry and report it

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A red patch that does not blanch is the first stage of a pressure sore, so the pressure is taken off it, he is turned often and the skin is kept clean and dry

🔍 Key Clues: 70-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — rub the area briskly: Rubbing damages the skin further

B — ask him to lie on the same side: Lying on the same side keeps the pressure exactly where it is

C — apply a hot water bottle: Heat increases the damage to the tissue

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse writes the stage and the site of the red patch on the chart and rechecks it every shift, because a sore that is found at stage one can still be reversed
option_2: ask him to lie on the same side
option_4: keep the area off pressure, turn him regularly, keep the skin clean and dry and report it

question: A 35-year-old man with a head injury has a rising blood pressure with a slowing pulse and irregular breathing. The nurse understands that this means:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. the pressure inside the skull is rising

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A rising blood pressure with a slowing pulse and irregular breathing is the response of the body to a rising pressure inside the skull and is a grave sign

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — he is improving: These are not signs of improvement

B — he needs more fluids: Giving more fluid does not treat the cause

D — he has a fever: A fever is a separate finding

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reports this combination at once and does not wait for the next scheduled round, because it is among the last warnings before the pressure becomes irreversible
option_3: the pressure inside the skull is rising

question: A 25-year-old woman at 38 weeks of pregnancy passes a small amount of blood stained mucus. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. reassure her that this is a show and that labour is near

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A show is the plug of mucus mixed with a little blood and it means that labour is approaching, which is normal at this stage

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — tell her to come back after a week: Telling her to stay away for a week is wrong when labour may begin at any time

B — treat it as a serious haemorrhage: A show is not a haemorrhage, unlike bleeding without mucus

D — prepare her for an immediate caesarean: A caesarean is not needed for a show

option_1: tell her to come back after a week
option_3: reassure her that this is a show and that labour is near

question: A woman ten days after delivery has a painful red breast with fever. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. apply a warm compress, help her empty the breast by feeding or expressing, give the ordered drugs and inform the doctor

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A painful red breast with fever is mastitis, and keeping the milk flowing with warmth and emptying the breast is the important part of the care

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — ask her to stop feeding altogether: Stopping the feeds makes the breast more engorged and the infection worse

C — apply ice and wait: Ice alone does not settle the infection and delays the treatment

D — bind the breast tightly: Tight binding is harmful and outdated

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse shows the mother how to fix the baby on the affected breast first, because an attachment that is corrected now prevents the same problem on the other side
option_1: apply a warm compress, help her empty the breast by feeding or expressing, give the ordered drugs and inform the doctor

question: In the second stage of labour the fetal heart rate stays at 100 per minute after a contraction. The nurse should first:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. turn her on her left side, give oxygen and inform the doctor at once

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A fetal heart rate that stays low after the contraction means the baby is short of oxygen, so the mother is turned on her left side, oxygen is given and the doctor is called at once

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — raise the head of the bed only: Raising the head end alone does not improve the blood flow to the placenta as the left lateral position does

C — wait for the next contraction: Waiting lets the distress continue

D — ask the mother to push harder: Pushing harder reduces the oxygen further

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse stays with the mother and keeps counting the fetal heart every few minutes, because the decision to deliver at once is taken on the pattern and not on a single reading
option_1: raise the head of the bed only
option_2: turn her on her left side, give oxygen and inform the doctor at once

question: Several people in a village have fever with chills returning on every third day. The nurse suspects:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. malaria

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A fever that returns on the third day with chills is the classic pattern of malaria from one of the species of the parasite

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — leprosy: Leprosy does not cause this kind of fever

B — tuberculosis: Tuberculosis gives an evening rise of fever with a cough

D — typhoid: Typhoid gives a continuing fever that rises step by step

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse collects a blood film during the chill, because the parasites are easiest to find in the blood at that hour

question: A 40-year-old man in a village has had a cough for three weeks with an evening rise of fever and loss of weight. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. collect two sputum samples for examination, send them to the laboratory and refer him under the tuberculosis programme

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A cough lasting three weeks with fever and weight loss is suspected tuberculosis, so the sputum is examined and the man is sent to the programme at once

🔍 Key Clues: 40-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — advise him to stop smoking only: Advice about smoking is useful but does not remove the infection

C — give a cough syrup and review after a month: A cough syrup delays the treatment and spreads the infection

D — reassure him that a long cough is common: A long cough with these signs is never merely common

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse asks about the other members of the household and gets them screened, because the person who sleeps in the same room is the one most likely already infected
option_2: collect two sputum samples for examination, send them to the laboratory and refer him under the tuberculosis programme
option_3: give a cough syrup and review after a month
option_4: reassure him that a long cough is common

question: An outbreak of cholera in a village is controlled best by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. providing safe water, safe disposal of excreta and early oral rehydration of every case

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Cholera spreads through contaminated water and food, so safe water, safe disposal of waste and prompt rehydration of the patients stop the spread and save lives

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — advising the people to eat less: Eating less increases the weakness and does not stop the spread

B — closing the village school only: Closing the school helps a little but does not reach the source

C — giving an antibiotic to the whole village: An antibiotic for the whole village is not the method and breeds resistance

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse finds out the common source of drinking water and gets it disinfected first, because in such an outbreak every case has drunk from the same place
option_3: giving an antibiotic to the whole village
option_4: providing safe water, safe disposal of excreta and early oral rehydration of every case

question: A 2-month-old baby is brought for the first set of vaccines. Before giving them the nurse must first:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. check that the baby is well, alert and free of fever

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The nurse checks the baby's general condition, the temperature and the weight before the vaccines are given

question: A 3-year-old child with fever and a rash is irritable and refuses all food and drink. The nurse should first:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. check for the danger signs such as lethargy, sunken eyes, a slow skin pinch and a cold extremity, and inform the doctor

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Refusal of food and drink with irritability calls for a check of the danger signs, which tell whether the child is seriously ill

🔍 Key Clues: 3-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — wait for the fever to settle: Waiting lets a serious illness progress unseen

C — force the child to eat: Forcing food in a sick child causes vomiting and choking

D — send the child home with a syrup: Sending such a child home with a syrup may cost the child's life

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

option_1: check for the danger signs such as lethargy, sunken eyes, a slow skin pinch and a cold extremity, and inform the doctor
option_4: send the child home with a syrup

question: A newborn has not passed meconium within the first twenty four hours. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. inform the doctor, watch for a distended abdomen and any vomiting and examine the anus for patency

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A delay in passing meconium may mean a block or an imperforate anus, so the doctor is told, the abdomen and the anus are checked and the baby is watched for vomiting

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give a glycerine suppository without an order: A suppository is not given without an order

B — wait for two more days: Waiting may allow a serious block to go on unnoticed

C — give a laxative: A laxative is never given to a newborn for this

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records the first stool with its time and character, because the passage of meconium within a day is one of the first proofs that the bowel is open
option_1: give a glycerine suppository without an order
option_4: inform the doctor, watch for a distended abdomen and any vomiting and examine the anus for patency

question: A 50-year-old man is given morphine for severe pain after surgery. The most important thing for the nurse to watch afterwards is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. his respiratory rate and depth

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Morphine depresses the breathing, and the rate and depth of respiration are watched closely after every dose

🔍 Key Clues: 50-year-old

question: In a row of 25 students a girl is ninth from the left end. Her position from the right end is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 17th

🧠 Method: The position from the right is the total plus one minus the position from the left, so 25 plus 1 minus 9 gives 17

⚡ Fast Approach: Positions add up to one more than the total number in the row.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 18th: 18 would need 8 from the left

B — 15th: 15 would need a position of 11 from the left

D — 16th: 16 would need 10 from the left

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Remember that the two positions count the same student twice, and add the one before subtracting

question: All nurses are caring. Some caring people are teachers. Which of the following follows?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Some caring people are nurses

🧠 Method: Since all nurses are caring, it follows that some caring people are nurses, which is only the same statement read the other way

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — No teacher is caring: It contradicts the second statement

C — Some nurses are teachers: Nothing links the nurses and the teachers, so this does not follow

D — All teachers are nurses: All teachers need not be nurses

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Draw two circles for the statements and ask whether the conclusion must be true in every possible arrangement, because a conclusion that is only sometimes true does not follow
